title: Solidigm picks Goldman and Morgan Stanley to lead US IPO amid AI storage boom - CHOSUNBIZ
source_used: Chosun Biz (Korean outlet) text, which credits Bloomberg citing multiple sources. Bloomberg original not found in Google News.
key_facts: Solidigm is the US NAND flash subsidiary of SK hynix, formed after SK hynix bought Intel's NAND flash and SSD business.
Bloomberg, citing multiple sources, reports Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters; JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup and UBS are also said to have joined.
A US listing is said to be pursued as early as 2027; Bloomberg, citing sources, says the IPO could raise about $10 billion.
Bloomberg earlier reported the valuation at listing could reach up to $100 billion.
SK hynix says nothing has been finalised regarding a US listing and that it is reviewing several options, including its own funds and external capital.
Demand driver: AI data centres are raising demand for enterprise high-capacity solid-state drives.
quote_evidence: On the 8th, Bloomberg, citing multiple sources, reported that Solidigm selected Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters for the IPO.
However, SK hynix said nothing has been finalized regarding Solidigm's U.S. listing.
We are reviewing several options, including using our own funds and external capital, but nothing has been decided at this time.
why_it_matters_hint: AI storage demand reaching the stock market; plan not settled.
notes: Bloomberg original not found in Google News (5-day search). Chosun Biz page read and used as the link. Score lowered 6 to 5: the headline says Solidigm 'picks' the banks as fact, but the account rests on Bloomberg's sources and SK hynix says nothing is final. Other copies seen, not read: Businesskorea, BigGo Finance, Korea Times.
